summary: The article is highly reliable, with all key factual claims verified against authoritative sources, primarily the Reserve Bank of India's press releases and official reports.

claims.claim: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) launched these surveys on September 8, 2026.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the RBI launched the surveys on September 8, 2026.

claims.claim: The results will be used for the next monetary policy review, scheduled for October 7, 2026.
claims.note: Several sources confirm the next bi-monthly monetary policy is scheduled for October 7, 2026.

claims.claim: The Inflation Expectations Survey of Households (IESH): This survey asks people in 19 cities about their personal understanding and expectations of price changes.
claims.note: The RBI's press release for the IESH explicitly states it covers 19 cities.

claims.claim: India's retail inflation, measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI), was 4.45% in July 2026, which is within the RBI's comfort zone of 2-6% but above its target of 4%.
claims.note: Multiple news reports confirm India's retail inflation was 4.45% in July 2026. The RBI's inflation target is 4% with a +/- 2% tolerance band (2-6%).

claims.claim: The Urban Consumer Confidence Survey (UCCS): This survey collects qualitative responses from households in 19 cities.
claims.note: The RBI's press release for the UCCS confirms it is conducted in 19 cities.

claims.claim: The Rural Consumer Confidence Survey (RCCS): Similar to the UCCS, this survey gathers views from households in rural and semi-urban areas across 31 states and Union Territories.
claims.note: The RBI's press release for the RCCS confirms its coverage across 31 states/UTs.

article_title: Your Everyday Spending and Mood: How RBI's Surveys Help Shape India's Economy
